Jade: I'm at the ticket hall. Are you waiting on platform six?
Owen: No. The announcement has changed our platform to eight. I'm standing beside the stairs.
Jade: Is our express train still leaving at ten thirty?
Owen: It is running fifteen minutes late. The display now says ten forty-five.
Jade: Did the announcement explain the delay?
Owen: Yes. Staff are checking a signal beside the track near North Junction. They cannot say when it will be ready.
Jade: I don't want to cancel our journey, but we will miss our connection at North Junction. Shall we use a direct service instead?
Owen: Yes. The conductor says the eleven o'clock service goes directly to the coast. We won't need a transfer.
Jade: Is our ticket valid on that service?
Owen: Yes, but our seat reservation is not. We can ask for new seats at the desk.
Jade: I'd like a seat near the luggage space. This suitcase is heavy.
Owen: There are two seats together in carriage five. The fare is the same, so we don't need to pay extra.
Jade: Good. What is the new arrival time?
Owen: Twelve ten. I'll message our friend now. She is meeting us outside the station.
Jade: What if she gets there early?
Owen: The terminal has an indoor waiting room. She can wait there and come outside when our train arrives.
Jade: Thanks. I'm buying some water before we board. Do you want anything?
Owen: Just water. Please meet me by the stairs at ten fifty. We should allow ten minutes to get to the right carriage.
Jade: All right. I'll check the platform display again before I come.

listening.text:
Mara: Is your appointment still on Thursday, Leo?
Leo: Yes, at two forty in the afternoon. I checked it this morning because I had written down two different times.
Mara: Where is the reception desk in that building?
Leo: It is beside the green entrance. The patient form is available there, and I can ask them to check the spelling of my name.
Mara: Have you prepared your questions?
Leo: I have a small list. I want to describe a cough, a sore throat and a headache. I will not guess a temperature or say I have a fever if I have not measured it.
Mara: Good. What about the pain you mentioned yesterday?
Leo: I will describe where it is and when I first noticed it. I also wrote down a question about my stomach. The nurse can ask for any other information during the examination.
Mara: Is there a place to ask about a prescription?
Leo: Yes. There is a pharmacy across the street. I have a question about a word on a medicine label, but I will ask the professional there rather than guess.
Mara: Which word is it?
Leo: Dose. I will show the tablet package and ask what the label means. I will not decide what to take from the word alone.
Mara: Did you write down your allergy question as well?
Leo: Yes. My main question is what information they need. I will ask the nurse how to describe how I breathe and when I might recover. I will also ask for advice about my treatment.
Mara: I can wait for you after my dentist visit.
Leo: Thanks. Please meet me by the yellow bench at three thirty, not at the green entrance. I will text you if the time changes.

Ella: We have a budget of twenty-five pounds for the soup evening. Have you made a list, Ben?
Ben: Yes. We need two loaves of bread, one bag of rice, three packets of soup and one liter of juice. Let us take a basket.
Ella: How much is the bread?
Ben: Each loaf has a price of two pounds fifty. Two loaves cost five pounds in total. The rice is six pounds for the bag.
Ella: The label says two kilograms, so we do not need to weigh it. The smaller one-kilogram bag was out of stock. What about the soup?
Ben: Each packet costs two pounds. The quantity is three, so that is six pounds. The juice is two pounds.
Ella: Then our total before the reduction is nineteen pounds. There is a card saying the shop will discount this purchase by three pounds.
Ben: That leaves an amount of sixteen pounds to pay. We can afford it and save nine pounds from our budget.
Ella: I have a twenty-pound note in cash. Will you check the change and receipt with me?
Ben: Of course. We should get four pounds back. If the assistant gives us a coin, we will count it with the notes.
Ella: Shall we take that package of cups too?
Ben: No. It is expensive, and the hall already has cups. A cheap extra is still unnecessary if we do not need it.
Ella: Agreed. In the shop near my old home, prices were shown in dollars. Here the pound sign is easy to see.
Ben: Let us join the queue and then take the food to the hall. We can tell the others exactly how much we spend.

Asha: Did you visit the two apartments in the Riverside neighborhood, Omar?
Omar: Yes. The Pine Street apartment has a monthly rent of 650 pounds. The Cedar Street one costs 690.
Asha: Which one is more spacious?
Omar: Pine has the bigger bedroom, but the kitchen is smaller than Cedar's. The bathroom is private in both places.
Asha: Does Pine have any furniture?
Omar: Yes, a sofa and a small table. I checked the floor and took a picture of a stain on the ceiling. The wall is a pale color. There was no leak near the window when I visited.
Asha: What did the landlord say about heating?
Omar: Heating uses electricity. The electricity charge is included in the rent, and there is no gas supply in that apartment.
Asha: Did you ask about the deposit and the lease?
Omar: The draft contract lists a deposit of 300 pounds and a six-month lease. I want to read the agreement carefully and ask about any existing damage before I sign.
Asha: What about the Cedar place?
Omar: The ceiling is lower, but the window in the living room is larger. It is as quiet as Pine in the afternoon. The front door looks secure, though I will check it again.
Asha: When would you need to move?
Omar: The suggested date is Saturday. I have the address written here. First, I will ask whether the landlord can repair a loose cupboard door.
Asha: Do you have to decide today?
Omar: No. I can take the information home and compare the rooms, any other bill and the travel time before replying.

listening.text:
Jo: How was your interview at the neighborhood museum on Friday, Rina?
Rina: It was interesting. I went at eleven in the morning and spoke to the manager of the events department.
Jo: What position did you apply for?
Rina: The vacancy was for a weekend workshop assistant. I sent the application on Wednesday. The employer wanted someone to help visitors find materials.
Jo: Did you give an example of your experience?
Rina: Yes. I described a garden event where my colleague and I worked as a team. I showed a certificate from a short art course as one qualification. I also brought a copy of my application for the manager.
Jo: What did they ask about?
Rina: They asked how I would help a customer who arrived late. I said I would listen, check the task list and ask an employee if I was unsure.
Jo: Did they explain the pay?
Rina: Yes. The hourly wage was fourteen pounds. The manager also mentioned a monthly salary, but that was for a different full-time position.
Jo: Did you get a decision at the interview?
Rina: No. They will contact each candidate next Tuesday. My goal was to speak clearly, and I felt successful in giving my example.
Jo: What will you do while you wait?
Rina: I will resume my library volunteering on Sunday. I enjoy that service, and I want to build a reliable work routine for my career.
Jo: Did you ask about the first responsibility?
Rina: Yes. A new assistant starts by preparing tables before visitors arrive. I wrote it in my notes, because this opportunity could teach me a new skill.

listening.text:
Nora: Have you seen the weather forecast for our picnic by the lake? I am bringing the food, so I need to know where we will eat.
Ben: Yes. Saturday should be warm, around 22 degrees Celsius, but the afternoon might be rainy. The morning will be sunny according to the latest report.
Nora: There is a dark cloud above the lake already. I think it is going to rain before noon. Should we cancel everything?
Ben: I would wait. A cloud can pass quickly, and the wind is moving it toward the hills. Let's plan for both possibilities.
Nora: Good idea. If it stays dry, we will meet under the large tree at eleven. If rain starts, we will move to the cafe beside the path.
Ben: I will bring an umbrella and a cloth for the food. The cafe has room for eight people, and our group has only six.
Nora: What about a storm? Last summer we heard thunder during a walk, and then we saw lightning. I do not want anyone to stay outside in that situation.
Ben: If we hear thunder or see lightning, we will go straight inside. We can ask the cafe staff when it is safe to leave.
Nora: The lake looks very different in each season. In winter, fog sometimes hides the other side. I remember one cold, snowy visit when the ground was freezing.
Ben: I prefer spring. The climate here is mild, and even a windy day can feel pleasant. Today the humidity is high, though, so let us take plenty of water.
Nora: Agreed. The sunshine may return later, but we can enjoy lunch indoors too. I will send everyone the two meeting places by nine thirty.
Ben: Thanks. I will check the new report at ten and call you if anything changes.

Liam: Have you chosen an activity for the leisure club day next month?
Rosa: Not yet. I want a hobby I can share with my brother, but our fitness levels are different. He is a keen athlete, and I have only recently started to exercise.
Liam: Have you ever played tennis together?
Rosa: Yes, we have. We borrowed a racket each from the center last year, and I enjoyed it. He wants to try a different sport this time.
Liam: The gym has a beginner volleyball session at ten. Its coach says no experience is needed, and the equipment is included.
Rosa: That sounds good. My brother has already tried basketball, but I have never played volleyball. We could learn together.
Liam: There is also an aerobics class at twelve, followed by yoga at two. Both are indoors, so the weather will not matter.
Rosa: I enjoy music, but my brother prefers a game with a ball. Let's book the ten o'clock session. How much does it cost?
Liam: Six dollars for each person. The center asks visitors to book by Thursday, because the room is small.
Rosa: I will tell him tonight. Could we cycle there? He has a bicycle, and I can borrow one.
Liam: Yes, and please wear a helmet. You can leave the bikes next to the front door. There is also a place to jog or hike in the park afterward.
Rosa: Is there a competition at the stadium that day too? I would like to watch a match after our session.
Liam: Yes. The first game begins at four. You can be a spectator without paying, and the coach will explain the score.
Rosa: Great. I do not mind who will win or lose. It will be fun to see how each opponent works with their team.
Liam: The winner gets a small cup, but nobody has to be a champion to join the morning sessions.

June: Yes. First, let's connect the laptop to the wireless network. The internet is working, and I can open the club website in the browser.

June: No, this is a practice account. The username is printed on the lesson card, and the password is on a separate card. We will remove both cards after practice.

June: Open the one called Agenda Practice. Then add Friday's start time, which is six thirty. Before you save it, check that the room is number twelve.
Omar: Done. I will save a copy on the device. Should I upload it to the shared area now?
June: Yes, but use the practice area, not the real members' area. After you upload it, check that its name appears on the page.
Omar: I can see it. Can I download the blank form as well? I want offline access when I am traveling without a connection.
June: Of course. You do not need to install any new software for this form. The center staff update the program when necessary.
Omar: Should I send an email to the club today?
June: Wait until we check the real agenda tomorrow. For now, use the logout button before leaving the computer. Online notes can be useful, but we need to check them carefully.
Omar: Thanks. This technology is less confusing when we take one step at a time.

listening.text:
Maya: Have you decided on a course at the college yet?
Eli: I have chosen the evening science course. I want to learn more about the river near my home, and the curriculum includes a project about local water.
Maya: That sounds useful. Is the first lesson on Monday?
Eli: No, it is on Wednesday at seven. The adviser said the classroom is in the older building on campus, next to the library.
Maya: What will you do in the first week?
Eli: We will hear a short lecture about asking clear questions. Then we will have a seminar to discuss possible topics in small groups.
Maya: I enjoy reading about geography. I might join you to understand how the river changes through the town.
Eli: Please do. The teacher also offers a tutorial on Friday for students who need help with the assignment.
Maya: What is the assignment? An essay?
Eli: A short report. First we plan to do research using the library's books. Then we decide what information belongs in the report.
Maya: Will there be an experiment in a laboratory?
Eli: Not in the first week. Later, a biology teacher will show us how to observe water plants safely. A chemistry teacher will help another group.
Maya: I hope the homework is manageable. I work full time, and I want to avoid studying too late every night.
Eli: The teacher recommends two short study periods a week. The final assessment is a project and a discussion, not a long examination.
Maya: Good. Do I need a university degree to join?
Eli: No. A graduate I met said people with different levels of education are welcome. She also studied history and literature at the center.
Maya: I will register tomorrow, then. I plan to finish reading the course description tonight and ask about the fee before I pay.
Eli: Great. I will bring my notebook on Wednesday so we can compare ideas after the lecture.

listening.text:
Sara: Are you ready for our school's environment event next week?
Jon: Almost. It is on Thursday at two, and the hall is booked. I want visitors to understand how we can reduce waste at school.
Sara: I have made a sign about litter near the river. After lunch, paper and plastic are often left beside the path. We need to protect the wildlife there.
Jon: Good. We should explain that litter can harm a bird's habitat. I will ask the nature club to show a picture of one local species.
Sara: Shall we call the activity a cleanup? I have gloves for twelve students, and the rubbish will be collected in bags.
Jon: Yes, but first we will check the path with a teacher. The cleanup will start at three, after the hall discussion.
Sara: I also have a box for clean metal cans. In our school's program, those cans are accepted for recycling. Can we recycle plastic there too?
Jon: Only the bottles listed on the school notice. We should read the notice before we put anything in the box. Other garbage goes in the regular bin.
Sara: What about the old wood from the garden signs? Could we reuse it instead of buying new material?
Jon: Yes. It is kept in the storage room, and the art group will turn it into new signs. That is one sustainable choice we can explain.
Sara: I want to add a display about renewable energy. The science class has a small model that uses sunlight to power a lamp.
Jon: Bring it, please. We can put it beside the map of the lake and the ocean. The geography teacher is drawing arrows to show where the water goes.
Sara: I will make a second card about ecology and conservation, too. It can ask visitors how their choices affect a natural place.
Jon: Great. After the event, the ideas are read by the club, and we choose one to try the following month.

speakingModels.text: I usually check the timetable before I travel. Today I am waiting at the main terminal with a small suitcase. My destination is a town by the sea, but there is a delay. I am checking the new departure time and listening to the announcement. My ticket is valid on a direct service, so I do not need a transfer. I am asking the conductor about a seat reservation near the luggage space. My friend is meeting me at the station this afternoon. I am sending her the new arrival time so that she does not have to wait too long. Before I board, I will check the platform display once more.

I have an appointment at a community clinic next week. Before I go, I will write down the symptom I want to describe and the time I first noticed it. At reception, I will check my name and phone number. If I have a question about an allergy, I will put it on the same card. I might also ask a nurse what an examination involves. If a prescription has a word I do not understand, I can ask the pharmacy to explain the label. I will listen to the professional and take notes instead of guessing. My friend will wait outside, and I will send a message when the conversation is finished.

My friends and I have a budget for a small lunch. First, we will write a list and agree on the quantity of each item. I will check the price on every label and put the food in a basket. We need a few vegetables and a little oil, but we do not need a large package of cups. Before we pay, I will add the cost of the items and check the total. If there is a discount, I will check that it appears on the receipt. I may use cash, so I will count the change as well. We will save the money left over and decide together whether we can afford fruit.

I am comparing two apartments near my class. The first apartment has a larger bedroom, while the second has a more spacious kitchen. The monthly rent is lower at the first place, but I still need to ask about the electricity bill. I would also check whether the bathroom is private and whether the heating is included. Before I move, I want to read the lease and ask the landlord about any damage. I will take photographs of the wall and floor so I can discuss any marks clearly. The first place looks quiet enough for study, but I will compare the travel time and the full agreement before I decide.

Last month I saw a vacancy at a community center and sent an application. I wanted the position because I enjoy helping people find useful information. At the interview, the manager asked about my experience. I described a library event where a colleague and I worked as a team. My example showed that I could listen to a customer and finish a task carefully. I also asked about the wage and the first responsibility in the department. The employer did not give me a decision that day, so I wrote down the date for a reply. After the interview, I planned to resume volunteering and practice another example for my career goal.

I would like to have a picnic with my friends near a lake in spring. I will check the weather forecast the night before and again in the morning. I think the day will be warm, but it might be windy. If I see a dark cloud, I will take an umbrella. If it is going to rain, we will use a nearby cafe instead of sitting outside. We will go indoors immediately if we hear thunder or see lightning. I enjoy sunshine, but a little rain will not end our plan. The important thing is to tell everyone both meeting places before they leave home. Then nobody needs to wait in the wrong place.

I have tried several activities in my leisure time, but my favorite hobby is volleyball. I first played it with friends last year at a small gym. I have never joined a serious competition, and I do not worry much about the score. I enjoy exercise more when everyone helps the team. A coach showed us how to pass the ball safely, and the center provided the equipment. I have also watched a match as a spectator, which gave me some ideas for practice. I would like to cycle to the gym next time, so I will wear a helmet. My goal is to improve my fitness and enjoy time with friends.

I would like to prepare a document for my local club. First, I connect my device to a wireless network and open a browser. Then I visit the club website and use my own account. I type the notes with the keyboard and save a file in a folder. Before I upload the document, I check the date and the place. After I upload it, I look for the correct file name online. If the internet is unavailable, my offline copy still opens. I do not share my password in an email. When I finish, I use the logout button so that the next person cannot use my account.

I would like to take an evening course at a local college. I want to learn about geography because I enjoy reading about places and people. I plan to visit the campus to ask about the curriculum and the time of each lesson. A short lecture could introduce a topic, and a seminar could give students time to discuss it. I would like to do research about my neighborhood and write a report. I work during the day, so I want to avoid studying too late. I will finish my homework in two short sessions each week. If I need help with an assignment, I will ask the teacher for a tutorial.

I would like my community to organize a cleanup beside a river. The place is a habitat for wildlife, and litter can harm animals that live there. First, the path is checked by a local guide. Then rubbish is collected by volunteers wearing gloves. Clean metal cans and accepted plastic bottles are put into separate boxes for recycling. We can also reduce waste by bringing our own water bottles. After the cleanup, the group could reuse old wood to make signs asking visitors to keep the path clean. This action will not solve all pollution, but it may help people care for the environment. I hope children and adults can work together and continue the habit.
